args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The round_money function documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
per FIN-212, but the implementation actually used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing
the nightly test test_money.py::test_half_even to fail. Switch the
rounding mode to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent values round to the
nearest even cent (e.g. 2.675 -> 2.68, 2.665 -> 2.66).

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented ROUND_HALF_UP despite documenting banker's rounding.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: switched `round_money` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed, including the failing test `test_half_even` (2.675 -> 2.68, 2.665 -> 2.66).

- **Fix**: Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and changed `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (commit `08d3cd5986`).

transcript.content: The bug is clear: the docstring claims ROUND_HALF_EVEN but the code uses ROUND_HALF_UP. Let me fix it on a new branch.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Wait, test expects 2.675 -> 2.68 and 2.665 -> 2.66. With ROUND_HALF_EVEN on Decimal("2.675") quantized to 0.01: 2.675 → half, round to even → 2.68 (8 is even). 2.665 → 2.66 (6 even). Yes. Currently ROUND_HALF_UP gives 2.68 and 2.67 — fails on second.

Fix: change import and rounding to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.
